recipes.name: Slow Cooker Tamale Pie
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can kidney beans, drained and rinsed

steps.text: Place ground beef in a skillet over medium heat. Cook and stir beef until it is browned, about 10 minutes, breaking up meat as it cooks. Drain beef and place it into the slow cooker. Stir in kidney beans, enchilada sauce, and garlic powder.
In a bowl, combine corn bread mix with milk, egg, and butter, and stir until just mixed. Stir in Cheddar cheese. Spoon corn bread mixture over beef mixture in the slow cooker.
Set the cooker to Low, cover, and cook until corn bread topping is cooked through and set, about 5 hours.

raw_recipe.headline: Slow Cooker Tamale Pie
raw_recipe.description: This slow cooker tamale pie recipe takes ground beef, cooks it with beans, seasonings, and corn bread mix and turns it into a tamale pie dinner.

review.reviewBody: This is very good. I did tweak it a little since we like things spicy. First, I doubled the recipe since I have a large oval slow cooker. I added some sauteed diced onions and bell peppers plus some chopped jalapenos (from a can) to the meat mixture. I also added jalapenos to the cornbread mixture. Also, 2/3 cups of milk for 2 packages of corn bread mix was not enough so I just kept adding until it looked like the right consistency. Finally, because the topping didn't brown in the slow cooker, I removed the crock and put it in the oven on "broil" for a couple of minutes. I will definitely make this again.

I want to warn first time users of this recipe that it only took 3 hrs. on low in our Hamilton Beach slow cooker. I also tweaked the recipe. First I cooked and drained the meat. Next returned the meat to the skillet added a medium chopped onion, & one clove minced garlic. Sauteed this until the onion was transparent. We don't care for kidney beans so I substituted bush's mild chili beans. Added the enchilada sauce as directed & put in the bottom of the crockpot. In small skillet I sauteed 2 T chopped red bell bepper, 1 jalapeno chopped(seeds removed), & 1/4 med. onion chopped. Lastly I added 1/3 C frozen corn to th skillet & cooked it until just warm. Added the sauteed veggies to the cornbread toping mixture. Topped the meat mixture. Tweak it with what your family prefers. Just be sure to check it as your crockpot may cook fast like mine. I will definitely make it again.

Great recipe.. I've had this dish a couple times many many years ago, so when I seen the recipe... it took me back. Adding the kidney beans was great addition. I followed the recipe and after reading a few other reviews I decided to add jalapenos to spice it up and I doubled the ingredients to be sure I would have leftovers. I also cooked mines in oven on 400° for 1 hour! Thanks!

Made the following changes: sauteed diced onion and garlic with meat and seasoned with cumin. Also added a few sliced and diced jalapeno slices to bean mixture with 1 cup corn. Like Mexican cornbread so used that instead for even more flavor. I like it spicy!

Very yummy! -although I tweaked the recipe a bit based on other reviewer comments. Others said the bread was too much compared to meat mixture. I didn't want to add more meat so added veggies. Added about 1/3 C canned (Trader Joes) corn, 2.3 oz can sliced olives, 14.5 oz can of Trader Joes diced & fire roasted tomatoes with organic green chiles. As others I also sauteed onions with the ground beef and also threw in 2 frozen Dorot crushed garlic cubes (equiv 2 cloves). Used 12 oz bottle of Trader Joe's enchilada sauce. Also put shredded cheese on top of corn bread topping instead of mixed with it. Digital crock-pot ran for 8 hrs on low, then on warm for another 2 (no delay start). Family doesn't do too spicy & this came out perfect for us. Served w/dollop of sour cream to tame it when needed. Will next try making it vegetarian w/Morningstar Mealstarters & will report back. :)

This recipe is very tasty. The only thing I would suggest is not using a slow cooker to make it in. It's so much better if you bake it in the oven. I bake it at 350 for around 45 minutes or until the top is golden brown. Usually I add sliced black olives and onions to the meat mixture. It's so good baked, because the top is nice and crunchy, which is especially yummy if you sprinkle some shredded cheddar on top before you bake.

Loved this recipe! Did modify a bit, as others have. Sauteed onion, red bell pepper and half a fresh jalapeno pepper until translucent. Added beef to pot and browned. Added several shakes of Mrs. Dash Spicy. When browned, put beef mixture in crock pot, added a can of medium spicy enchilada sauce and one small can tomato paste. Also added half a bag of frozen corn and a small can of sliced black olives. I used 2 boxes of Jiff cornbread mix, 2 eggs and 2/3 cup of milk mixed, then added 1 cup cheddar cheese. I poured that on top of the beef already in the crock pot and put it on low for 4 hours. When it was done, I topped it with more cheddar cheese and more black olives and then put it under the broiler just to melt the cheese.

My husband loved this! I followed the recipe but added a 1/4 tsp of cayenne to add a bit of spice. I used Krusteaz cornbread mix as it has a bit of honey flavor. The combo of the spice and the sweet was superb. Served with a large spooonful of salsa. Next time will double the recipe for a large slow cooker when cooking for a crowd.

This came out just as it appears in the picture and tasted great. I used 1 lb grnd beef, 2 cans of beans (black and pink kidney) and a 1lb bag of jalepeno corn bread mix. To the beef, I ddded fresh green peppers, onions and garlic, cumin (a must), chili powder, 2 jalepenos and dash (or 4) of hot sauce. After draining beef, I added about 6T of Pace Chunky Medium salsa, which gave it some good flavor and 1.5 cups of enchilada sauce. Next time I will use more salsa and tomato sauce vs enchilada sauce from a can (yuck). Cooked it on low for about 4 hours. Really you can eyeball when it's done by looking at the cornbread, which for me had a nice hard crust on top and cooked solid.

Delicious..I tweeked it a bit. I used 1 1/2 lbs ground turkey and 2 boxes of corn bread mix. In my turkey I added a couple cloves crushed garlic, half a finely chopped jalepeno, half an onion, a can of black beans and my own taco seasoning. I stirred in the enchilada sauce. In my cornbread mix I added 1 egg , 1/3 cup milk, 3/4 cup sour cream, 1/2 cup cheese and 1/2 of a chopped jalepeno. It is so tweeked because I used 2 different recipes and combined the ideas. Lol I put it in the slow cooker onb medium /low for about 4.5 or 5 hrs and it turned out excellent. The leftovers are spectacular too!

With some modifications, this has fast become a favorite go-to for me.

Following other reviewers' suggestions, I double everything.

I also add sauteed onion, green bell pepper, olives and canned chopped jalapenos to the meat mixture.

Using medium spiciness enchilada sauce is worth the extra flavor, though it's harder to find.

Also, I don't really see much of a point in using the slow cooker for this--it's just as easy and way faster to pop it in the oven.
Easy to make and very good!
This recipe is great! We doubled the recipe and instead of using kidney beans, we added black beans and corn. It turned out to be a spectacular dinner!
I made this tonight and as others said I made some additions. I added half a onion chopped and half a can of Rotel mild . It was outstanding.

I made this as written with only two small changes. I added onion when the beef was almost brown, because we have onion in just about everything and I did not have red kidney beans as shown in the picture so I used white kidney beans. I divided the mixture into two smaller baking dishes, cooked both and froze one for another night, there is only 2 of us. I gave it only four stars because I think it needed something. May try adding green chilies next time, but will definitely make it again.
This was simple and yummy. I added sauteed onions and jalapeno peppers to the meat along with chili powder and cumin. Added hot sauce and sour cream to the plated dish. Very good and economical dish!

My family loved this football Sunday slow cooker entrée! I eliminated kidney beans, and replaced with canned corn. I also added diced chili peppers to the meat mixture, along with a can of Rotel tomatoes/chilis added to the corn bread in place of the milk. Turned out great!!
It was good. I did some tweaking also, doubled the recipe, used piquito beans and Kodiak corn bread mix. It could use a little salt. Great for leftovers
I would make this again. It's easy and delicious.
So I used a mix of ground beef with taco seasoning and Charley’s Slow Cooker Mexican Style Meat layered with the sauce and beans. Turned out fantastic!!
